{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -t 01:30:00
#   -N 3
#   --ntasks-per-node=4
#   --ntasks-per-socket=2
#   --gres=gpu:4
#   -c 4
#   --mem-per-cpu=0

flux alloc \
  -N 3 \
  -n 12 \
  -c 4 \
  --gpus=4 \
  --time=1h30m \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=0 (no memory limit / all memory) has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: memory placement/limits may differ; job may be placed where less memory is available or contend more.

# NOTE: Slurm --ntasks-per-socket=2 has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: task placement/NUMA locality may differ, potentially affecting performance.

export PYTHONHASHSEED=0

module load anaconda
source activate pppl
module load cudatoolkit/8.0
module load cudnn/cuda-8.0/6.0
module load openmpi/cuda-8.0/intel-17.0/2.1.0/64
module load intel/17.0/64/17.0.4.196 intel-mkl/2017.3/4/64

# remove checkpoints for a benchmark run
rm -f /tigress/$USER/model_checkpoints/*
rm -f /tigress/$USER/results/*
rm -f /tigress/$USER/csv_logs/*
rm -f /tigress/$USER/Graph/*
rm -f /tigress/$USER/normalization/*

export OMPI_MCA_btl="tcp,self,sm"

# NOTE: Slurm used srun to launch an MPI-enabled program. Flux MPI integration is site-specific;
# we cannot portably replicate srun semantics here.
# Performance implication: running without a parallel launcher may only execute one rank.
# Best-effort: use mpirun with the requested total task count.

mpirun -np 12 python mpi_learn.py
'
"
}
